region_name: Elwha Valley, Hurricane Ridge, Grand Valley & the Bailey Range
summary: The north-central Olympics: Hurricane Ridge's windy meadows (Hurricane Hill, Klahhane Ridge, Lake Angeles, Heather Park) where the day lodge burned in 2023 and a rebuild is not expected before 2028; Obstruction Point and the quota-limited lake camps of Grand Valley; and the Elwha, the park's largest watershed, whose dams came out in 2011-2014 and whose road has been closed to cars at Madison Falls since a washout, adding 6.5-8 walking or biking miles to Whiskey Bend and Boulder Creek. From the Elwha the trail runs 28 miles to Low Divide, with branches to Hayden Pass, Dodger Point Lookout, Olympic Hot Springs, Boulder Lake and Appleton Pass, and the off-trail Bailey Range Traverse links the High Divide to the Elwha headwaters for expert parties.

nodes.name: Olympic National Park Visitor Center & Wilderness Information Center (Port Angeles)
nodes.description: A low building at the foot of the mountains where rangers hand out maps, answer worried questions, and lend bear canisters from a shelf of black barrels. Everyone who sleeps in the high country starts their story here.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: wooden counter with a ranger in a flat hat and a row of black bear canisters. Midground: a big relief map of the peninsula on the wall. Background window: green foothills under a gray sky. Sky: light cyan with one white cloud.

nodes.name: Heart O' the Hills Trailhead (Lake Angeles / Heather Park)
nodes.description: A shady gravel lot just inside the park entrance, where two trails leave side by side into tall second-growth hemlock. One goes to a lake in a stone bowl; the other climbs and climbs toward a meadow in the sky.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: brown trail signboard with two arrows (LAKE ANGELES / HEATHER PARK). Midground: straight dark-green hemlock trunks, dithered moss. Background: hint of a steep green slope. Sky: almost hidden by canopy, a few cyan gaps.

nodes.name: Heart O' the Hills Campground
nodes.description: A year-round drive-in campground of 105 sites under old trees, five miles above Port Angeles and twelve below Hurricane Ridge: the place to sleep before an early start.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: picnic table and a small tent. Midground: huge mossy trunks and a car. Background: dark forest. Sky: dusk blue with first stars.

nodes.name: Halfway Rock
nodes.description: A great gray boulder left behind by a long-gone glacier sits beside the switchbacks, beard lichen dripping from the trees around it. It marks roughly the middle of the long climb to Heather Park.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: switchback trail. Midground: huge rounded gray boulder (glacial erratic) with lichen speckles. Background: hemlock trunks with pale green beard lichen. Sky: none, forest light.

nodes.name: Heather Park

camp.reservation_or_quota: Recreation.gov camp area "Heather Park (No Campfires)", Hurricane district; max group 12; not a quota-limited area in the Oct 2026 snapshot.
camp.water: Small creek running through the camps (only water on the Heather Park Trail); treat it.
camp.notes: Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain. Toilet listing conflicts: Recreation.gov says "use available toilet", NPS trail page says none. Rough, exposed tread continues above to Victor Pass; a trailhead sign warns that hikers have become lost there in darkness or fog.

nodes.description: A small hanging bowl of heather and grass tucked under the jagged tops of First and Second Top, with a trickle of ice-cold water and tents hidden among stunted firs. Above it the trail turns to loose gravel and thin air.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: purple-pink heather clumps and a tiny tent. Midground: bowl meadow with a thread of creek. Background: dark-gray rocky spires (First Top / Second Top). Sky: deep blue, dithered to cyan at the horizon.

nodes.name: Lake Angeles

camp.reservation_or_quota: Recreation.gov camp area "Lake Angeles (No Campfires)"; max group 12; not quota-limited in the Oct 2026 snapshot but very busy on summer weekends.
camp.water: Lake and its outlet stream; treat it.
camp.notes: Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain. Campsites are in forest at the north end. Toilet listing conflicts (Recreation.gov: use available toilet; NPS page: none). Trailhead parking full by ~9 am on summer weekends (WTA Aug 2026).

nodes.description: A teardrop of green water fills a deep cirque, with a single wooded island floating in the middle and gray cliffs rising almost straight to Klahhane Ridge. Waterfalls thread down the walls after snowmelt.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: rocky shore and a fallen log. Midground: emerald lake with a small dark-green island of firs. Background: tall gray cliff wall with white waterfall threads, ridge crest at top. Sky: narrow band of blue above the cliffs.

nodes.name: Klahhane Ridge (Lake Angeles Trail junction)
nodes.description: The high knob where the ridge path meets the steep, dusty drop to Lake Angeles. Wind pours over the crest; to the north the Strait glitters, to the south the whole crumpled interior of the Olympics stands up white and blue.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: windswept rocky crest with a small cairn and signpost. Midground: far below, a tiny green lake in a cirque. Background: rows of snowy peaks to the south. Sky: bright blue with streaming wind clouds; distant strip of sea and a white volcano (Mount Baker) to the northeast.

nodes.name: Victor Pass (Switchback / Heather Park / Klahhane Ridge junction)
nodes.description: A notch below the tilted, layered rock of Mount Angeles where three trails meet. Marmots whistle from the scree and the meadows are bright with paintbrush and lupine in midsummer.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: trail junction post. Midground: green and magenta meadow with gray scree. Background: Mount Angeles with tilted red-and-gray rock bands. Sky: blue, a hawk silhouette.

nodes.name: Switchback Trailhead
nodes.description: A small pullout on the winding Hurricane Ridge Road. The trail wastes no time: it zigzags straight up the slope like a stitched seam.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: road edge with a parked car and trail sign. Midground: steep forested slope with a zigzag path. Background: open meadow ridge above. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Klahhane Ridge Trail / Switchback Trail junction
nodes.description: Where the long, gentle ridge path from Hurricane Ridge meets the steep Switchback Trail. From here it is a mile of hard climbing to Victor Pass.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: brown signpost with two arrows. Midground: subalpine firs and meadow. Background: Mount Angeles above. Sky: blue with puffy clouds.

nodes.name: Mount Angeles
nodes.description: A rugged three-summited peak of tilted volcanic and sedimentary rock that looms over Port Angeles. Its top is a scramble, not a hike: loose gullies, late snow, and a long way down.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: steep gray scree gully with a scrambler using hands. Midground: rotten snow patch. Background: the town and harbor far below, the Strait and Vancouver Island. Sky: pale blue.

nodes.name: Hurricane Ridge Visitor Center (site of the burned Day Lodge)
nodes.description: A big parking lot on a windy crest, with meadows full of grazing deer and the whole Olympic range lined up across the valley. The old day lodge burned in 2023; today there are portable toilets and trailers instead of a building.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: asphalt lot edge, a blacktail deer, small temporary trailer and porta-potties. Midground: green meadow with subalpine fir spires. Background: wall of white peaks (Mount Olympus and the Bailey Range). Sky: dithered blue to cyan, one long cloud.

nodes.name: Wolf Creek Trailhead (Hurricane Hill Road picnic area)
nodes.description: A picnic area a mile down the Hurricane Hill Road where an old trail slips off the ridge and begins an eight-mile descent through forest to the Elwha.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: picnic table and trail sign WOLF CREEK. Midground: subalpine firs dropping away. Background: deep blue valley and far ridges. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Hurricane Hill Trailhead
nodes.description: The end of the narrow road west of Hurricane Ridge, a small lot that fills quickly. A wide paved path heads off toward a bald, grassy summit.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: small parking lot and a paved path. Midground: rounded grassy hill with a few firs. Background: peaks of the Bailey Range. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Hurricane Hill Trail / Little River Trail junction
nodes.description: Early on the paved Hurricane Hill path a faint dirt trail drops north into the trees toward the Little River, eight miles and four thousand feet below.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: pavement edge and a narrow dirt path. Midground: firs and grass. Background: the Strait of Juan de Fuca. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Hurricane Hill Trail / Elwha to Hurricane Hill Trail junction
nodes.description: Just below the summit a trenched dirt trail tips off the west side of the hill and plunges toward the Elwha valley, more than five thousand feet down.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: trail split with a small sign. Midground: golden grass slope falling away. Background: deep Elwha valley and the Bailey Range. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Hurricane Hill
nodes.description: A bald, wind-polished summit with signs naming every peak on the horizon. Ferries crawl across the Strait to Canada on one side; on the other the Bailey Range shines with snow.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: summit plaque and bench, tufts of golden grass. Midground: rolling green ridges. Background left: blue Strait with a tiny white ferry and Vancouver Island; right: snowy Bailey Range and Mount Olympus. Sky: brilliant blue, dithered.

nodes.name: Little River Trailhead
nodes.description: A small lot on a rural road outside the park, where a quiet trail follows a mossy little river upstream before climbing hard to Hurricane Hill.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: gravel lot and a footbridge. Midground: mossy maples over a clear stream. Background: forested slopes. Sky: soft gray-blue.

nodes.name: Little River Trail at the park boundary
nodes.description: Somewhere along the stream the trail passes from state land into the national park: same moss, same ferns, but now a wilderness permit is needed to sleep here.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: small brown boundary sign on a post. Midground: ferns and big cedars. Background: stream glints. Sky: green canopy.

nodes.name: PJ Lake Trailhead (Waterhole, Obstruction Point Road)
nodes.description: A tiny pullout on the narrow gravel Obstruction Point Road. The trail starts gently and then drops off the world into a steep basin.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: dusty gravel road with a pullout. Midground: subalpine firs at the lip of a basin. Background: Strait of Juan de Fuca and Mount Baker. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: PJ Lake

camp.reservation_or_quota: Recreation.gov camp area "P.J. Lake (No Campfires)"; not quota-limited in the Oct 2026 snapshot.
camp.water: Lake and inlet streams; treat it.
camp.notes: Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain. Two sites per WTA: one large site at the shore and one in the firs. Toilet: none listed.

nodes.description: A small, cold tarn at the bottom of a steep basin, where trout ring the surface and a thin waterfall drops through mossy rock below the outlet. Red-capped mushrooms dot the forest floor in late summer.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: red-and-white toadstools and a mossy log. Midground: small blue-green lake with rings from rising fish. Background: steep forested basin wall with a rock knob above. Sky: small patch of blue.

nodes.name: Obstruction Point Trailhead
nodes.description: The end of an eight-mile ribbon of gravel, perched above timberline. Treeless ridges run off in three directions and the glaciers of Mount Olympus fill the western sky.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: dusty lot with a pit toilet and a signboard. Midground: barren gray-green ridge with a trail line. Background: distant white glaciated massif (Mount Olympus). Sky: deep blue at top, dithered lighter near horizon.

nodes.name: Lillian Ridge (Grand Valley Trail / Lillian Ridge Way Trail junction)
nodes.description: The high point of the walk along Lillian Ridge, where the main trail tips over and dives toward Grand Valley and a fainter way trail keeps running along the crest. No water anywhere up here, only wind and view.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: rocky ridge crest with low alpine plants. Midground: steep drop into a green valley with two blue lakes. Background: rows of peaks and Mount Olympus. Sky: blue, a raven.

nodes.name: Lillian Ridge Way Trail / Grand Pass Trail junction (south of Gladys Lake)
nodes.description: Above Gladys Lake the steep way trail from Lillian Ridge rejoins the main path to Grand Pass.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: faint path meeting a clearer trail. Midground: meadow benches with snow patches. Background: the cirque below Grand Pass. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Grand Lake

camp.reservation_or_quota: QUOTA AREA (Grand Valley). Recreation.gov "Grand Lake (No Campfires)": 7 groups / 20 people per night (Oct 2026 snapshot); max group 6. Grand Valley reservation season Jul 1 - Oct 15, 2026.
camp.water: Grand Lake and Grand Creek; giardia present, treat all water.
camp.notes: Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain. Solar composting toilet (NPS). Designated sites only in Grand Valley. Sites are a little hard to find: follow the path around the shore (WTA Jul 2026). Fish in the lake. Habituated deer try to steal food.

nodes.description: The largest of the Grand Valley lakes lies in a forested hollow at the foot of a long meadow, its surface flecked with rising trout. Deer wander boldly among the tents at dusk.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: shoreline rocks and a fishing pole. Midground: oval blue lake framed by spire-shaped subalpine firs. Background: green valley sweeping up to rocky ridges. Sky: blue with puffy clouds; deer silhouette at shore.

nodes.name: Moose Lake

camp.reservation_or_quota: QUOTA AREA (Grand Valley). Recreation.gov "Moose Lake (No Campfires)": 6 groups / 22 people per night (max 6 per group) plus "Moose Lake Group Site" 1 group of 7-12 (Oct 2026 snapshot). Season Jul 1 - Oct 15, 2026.
camp.water: Moose Lake and nearby creek; treat (giardia).
camp.notes: Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain. Solar composting toilet (NPS). Only designated group site in Grand Valley for parties of 7-12.

nodes.description: An open meadow lake higher in the valley, with wide views up toward Grand Pass and little creeks chattering past the campsites. Marmots sun themselves on the boulders.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: grassy bank with a tent. Midground: blue lake with meadow shores and scattered firs. Background: rocky headwall and the notch of Grand Pass. Sky: blue, a few clouds.

nodes.name: Gladys Lake

camp.reservation_or_quota: QUOTA AREA (Grand Valley). Recreation.gov "Gladys Lake (No Campfires)": 4 groups / 10 people per night (Oct 2026 snapshot); max 6 per group. Season Jul 1 - Oct 15, 2026.
camp.water: Gladys Lake and snowmelt streams; treat.
camp.notes: Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain. No toilet: dig a cat hole or use the Moose Lake toilet about a mile away (Recreation.gov).

nodes.description: The smallest and highest of the valley lakes, a cold mirror ringed by heather and late snow, just below the switchbacks to Grand Pass.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: heather and a snowbank. Midground: small round tarn reflecting peaks. Background: steep switchbacks to a pass. Sky: blue fading to pink (sunset palette option).

nodes.name: Grand Pass
nodes.description: A high, rocky saddle at the head of Grand Valley. On one side the lakes you camped by shine like coins; on the other the trail plunges two thousand feet to Cameron Creek. A short scramble leads to Grand Pass Peak for an even bigger view.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: talus saddle with a cairn. Midground left: green valley with three tiny lakes; right: deep forested gorge. Background: glaciers of Mount Olympus and Mount Cameron. Sky: dark blue at top, white clouds below the peaks.

nodes.name: Badger Valley
nodes.description: A quiet, curving valley floor where the loop trail bottoms out among cow parsnip, thistle and arnica before beginning the long climb back toward Obstruction Point. Marmot burrows pock the tread.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: trail through tall white cow parsnip and yellow arnica. Midground: valley floor with a creek. Background: steep scree slopes rising to a ridge. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Badger Valley Trail / Elk Mountain Trail junction
nodes.description: About a mile below the trailhead a primitive trail branches up to the crest of Grand Ridge and Elk Mountain.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: signpost. Midground: scree field with a marmot on a rock. Background: ridge crest. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Badger Valley Trail / Grand Ridge (Obstruction Point-Deer Park) Trail junction
nodes.description: Just east of the trailhead the Badger Valley trail leaves the Grand Ridge path and drops away into the valley.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: barren ridge path. Midground: lingering snow patch. Background: Badger Valley below. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Lake Lillian

camp.reservation_or_quota: Recreation.gov cross-country camp area "Lake Lillian (No Campfires)" (Hurricane district); 0 permits available in the Oct 2026 snapshot (not offered online; contact the WIC).
camp.notes: Off-trail destination below McCartney Peak; no maintained route. Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain.

nodes.description: A remote high lake in rock and snow at the head of the Lillian River, reached only by cross-country travel from Lillian Ridge.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: talus and snow. Midground: small turquoise lake with ice floes. Background: dark crags of McCartney Peak. Sky: blue-black at zenith.

nodes.name: Madison Falls Trailhead (Elwha road gate)
nodes.description: The last place a car can go in the Elwha. Beyond the gate the old road runs on for miles, cracked and mossy, used now only by hikers and bicycles; a short paved path leads to a lacy sixty-foot waterfall.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: metal gate across the road, a bicycle leaning on it. Midground: paved path to a white waterfall in mossy rock. Background: tall maples and firs. Sky: gray-blue, soft.

nodes.name: Whiskey Bend Road junction / Elwha to Hurricane Hill Trailhead (old Elwha Ranger Station)
nodes.description: Past the washed-out bend of the river the road splits by the shuttered old ranger station: left climbs Whiskey Bend Road toward the Elwha trail, right crosses the river toward Glines Canyon and the hot springs. A steep trail starts here for Hurricane Hill, five thousand feet up.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: cracked asphalt fork with an old wooden sign. Midground: small historic ranger cabin with closed shutters. Background: forested valley walls. Sky: blue-gray.

nodes.name: Glines Canyon Spillway Overlook
nodes.description: A walkway on the stump of a vanished dam, 210 feet above a narrow gorge. Where a reservoir once sat, a young forest now grows over the old lakebed and the free river roars below.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: concrete spillway railing with an interpretive sign. Midground: deep narrow rock canyon with white water. Background: green alder flats where Lake Mills used to be, mountains beyond. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Happy Lake Ridge Trailhead (Olympic Hot Springs Road)
nodes.description: A trail sign beside the empty upper road marks where a dry ridge path begins a long climb toward Happy Lake.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: mossy asphalt and a trail sign. Midground: madrona and fir. Background: ridge above. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Boulder Creek Trailhead (old Olympic Hot Springs road end)
nodes.description: The old road end, eight miles past the gate, where bikes must be left at the wilderness boundary. The roadbed narrows into a trail that smells faintly of sulfur.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: bike rack and wilderness sign. Midground: old roadbed turning into trail. Background: forested slopes. Sky: blue-gray.

nodes.name: Olympic Hot Springs
nodes.description: Across a bridge over Boulder Creek, little pools of warm, sulfur-smelling water steam among the ferns where a resort stood a century ago. Some are bath-warm, some far too hot to touch.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: small rock-ringed pool with rising steam (dithered white). Midground: ferns, moss and a footbridge over a creek. Background: dark forest slope. Sky: hazy gray-blue.

nodes.name: Boulder Creek Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Recreation.gov "Boulder Creek (No Campfires)"; max group 12; not quota-limited in the Oct 2026 snapshot.
camp.water: No easy water in camp: get it from Crystal Creek before camp or a few minutes up the Appleton Pass trail; take Boulder Creek water above the hot-spring inflow; treat.
camp.notes: Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain. Year-round burn ban at Boulder Creek / Olympic Hot Springs. Bear-wire cables were being decommissioned (WTA Sept 26, 2026). NPS reports a potentially habituated bear around the camp (6/14/26). Former drive-in campground on a flat bench.

nodes.description: A big, quiet flat in the forest where cars once parked, now slowly being reclaimed by alders and moss. Bear wires hang unused; a black bear has been seen nosing around.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: tent on a flat clearing, a black bear canister. Midground: alders and an old picnic-area outline. Background: tall firs; distant ridge glimpsed. Sky: small patch of blue.

nodes.name: Boulder Lake Trail / Appleton Pass Trail junction
nodes.description: Under big firs the trail forks: one branch climbs toward Boulder Lake, the other follows Boulder Creek up past waterfalls toward Appleton Pass.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: signpost and roots. Midground: forest with sword ferns. Background: sound of falls suggested by white streak. Sky: none.

nodes.name: Boulder Lake

camp.reservation_or_quota: Recreation.gov "Boulder Lake (No Campfires)"; max group 12; not quota-limited in the Oct 2026 snapshot.
camp.water: Boulder Lake, Boulder Creek and nearby streams; treat.
camp.notes: Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain. Pit toilet. Lake holds non-native brook trout; fishing allowed. Camp on bare ground only.

nodes.description: A subalpine lake under the gray shoulder of Boulder Peak, its shore littered with the giant stones that gave it a name. Brook trout dimple the water in the evening.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: big gray boulders at the water edge. Midground: dark blue lake. Background: rocky peak (Boulder Peak) with snow streaks. Sky: blue to orange at sunset.

nodes.name: Boulder Lake / Happy Lake Ridge Trail junction
nodes.description: Just above Boulder Lake the Happy Lake Ridge trail climbs away north onto the dry crest.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: junction sign. Midground: firs and huckleberry. Background: ridge. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Aurora Ridge Primitive Trail / Happy Lake Ridge Trail junction
nodes.description: On the open crest of Happy Lake Ridge an even rougher path heads west along Aurora Ridge toward Lake Crescent.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: meadow crest. Midground: rolling ridgeline. Background: Mount Olympus to the south. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Happy Lake Ridge Trail / Happy Lake Trail junction
nodes.description: The high point of the ridge walk, where a short spur drops to Happy Lake in its little forested bowl.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: signpost on a grassy knoll. Midground: lake glimpsed below. Background: far peaks. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Happy Lake

camp.reservation_or_quota: Recreation.gov "Happy Lake (No Campfires)"; max group 12 per Recreation.gov (NPS map lists 1-6); not quota-limited in the Oct 2026 snapshot.
camp.water: Happy Lake (fill up here: much of the ridge trail is dry); treat.
camp.notes: Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain.

nodes.description: A small lake in a forested basin below the ridge, the only sure water for miles along a dry, sunny crest.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: tent among firs. Midground: small still lake. Background: forested slope. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Whiskey Bend Trailhead
nodes.description: The quiet end of Whiskey Bend Road, where the long Elwha River Trail begins. With the road closed to cars, only walkers and cyclists arrive here now, and the forest feels very big.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: wide trail entering forest beside a big trailhead signboard. Midground: tall firs and maples. Background: glimpse of the valley. Sky: pale blue through canopy.

nodes.name: Rica Canyon Trail junction
nodes.description: A side trail drops steeply toward the river and the rock gate of Goblins Gate.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: sign RICA CANYON / GOBLINS GATE. Midground: trail plunging into ferns. Background: forest. Sky: none.

nodes.name: Goblins Gate
nodes.description: The whole Elwha squeezes through a dark slot of rock here and boils into a deep green pool. People say the rock walls look like grimacing faces.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: wet rock ledge. Midground: narrow black rock gap with churning white-and-green water. Background: mossy trees leaning over. Sky: thin slit of blue.

nodes.name: Krause Bottom Trail junction
nodes.description: A connector trail tumbles down to the river flats of Krause Bottom.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: signpost. Midground: maples. Background: river light. Sky: none.

nodes.name: Krause Bottom

camp.reservation_or_quota: Recreation.gov camp area "Krause Bottom-Rica Canyon"; not quota-limited in the Oct 2026 snapshot.
camp.notes: Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain. Fires only in existing rings below 3,500 ft when no ban is in effect. Stage 2 fire restrictions (all campfires banned parkwide) were in effect from Aug 11, 2026; no lifting notice found by Oct 7, 2026. A 2026 trip report could not find the mapped camp areas in Geyser Valley.

nodes.description: An alder-shaded river flat where homesteaders once cleared fields. Salmon, back after the dams came out, hold in the riffles in late summer.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: grassy flat with an old split-rail remnant. Midground: alder grove. Background: wide gravel-bar river. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Michael's Cabin
nodes.description: A weathered log cabin at a three-way junction, once home to a trapper the locals called Cougar Mike. Here the Humes Ranch loop drops toward the river and the main trail carries on south.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: three-way signpost. Midground: small gray log cabin with a shake roof, open doorway. Background: big-leaf maples with moss. Sky: dappled.

nodes.name: Humes Ranch

camp.reservation_or_quota: Recreation.gov "Humes Ranch"; max group 12; not quota-limited in the Oct 2026 snapshot.
camp.water: Elwha River (some river access is through other campsites); treat.
camp.notes: Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain. Fires allowed only in established rings with dead and down wood, and only when no seasonal ban: Stage 2 fire restrictions (all campfires banned parkwide) were in effect from Aug 11, 2026; no lifting notice found by Oct 7, 2026. Toilet listing conflicts (NPS camp map: yes; Recreation.gov and NPS trail page: dig a cat hole). Bears and cougars frequent the meadow (2026 reports).

nodes.description: A sunny meadow above the river where a homestead cabin from about 1900 still stands, with old fruit trees gone wild in the grass. Deer graze at dusk, and sometimes something with yellow eyes watches them.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: tall meadow grass and an old apple tree. Midground: historic log cabin with a porch and stone chimney. Background: forested canyon walls of the Elwha. Sky: golden evening light.

nodes.name: Long Ridge Trail junction (Humes Ranch loop) and Dodger Point Bridge
nodes.description: Past the ranch meadow the trail meets a sturdy bridge over the Elwha at the mouth of its Grand Canyon. Across it, the Long Ridge Trail begins a thirteen-mile climb toward a lookout in the sky.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: wooden footbridge deck. Midground: emerald river in a rock canyon below. Background: steep forested ridge rising. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Dodger Point junction (Long Ridge Trail / lookout spur / Ludden Peak Way Trail)
nodes.description: A low spot on the ridge below the lookout where trails split: up to the lookout, south toward Ludden Peak and the Bailey Range, or back down the long ridge home.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: signpost on a heather saddle. Midground: meadow with tarns. Background: Mount Ferry and Stephen Peak with snow, Mount Olympus behind. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Dodger Point (Lookout)

camp.reservation_or_quota: Recreation.gov "Dodger Point (No Campfires)"; max group 6; not quota-limited in the Oct 2026 snapshot. Separate cross-country zone "Dodger Point Trail".
camp.water: Recreation.gov: no water at the camp. In practice a small stream crosses the path to the campground and tarns lie below the point, but flow can be very low by midsummer; last reliable water on Long Ridge was ~3.5 mi below the spur (Aug 2026).
camp.notes: Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain. Camp sits just below the 1933 fire lookout (on the National Register).

nodes.description: A tiny wooden lookout built in 1933 perches on a rocky point in the very middle of the park. From its shuttered windows the valleys fall away in every direction and Mount Olympus fills the southwest like a frozen wave.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: heather and rocks on the summit. Midground: small square shuttered lookout cabin with a pyramid roof. Background: glaciated Mount Olympus and Bailey Range peaks, deep blue valleys. Sky: dithered sunset orange-to-purple option; stars at night.

nodes.name: Ludden Peak Way Trail / Dodger Point Primitive Trail junction
nodes.description: On the slope below the lookout an unmaintained trail dives east toward the river and Remann's Cabin, while a narrow, crumbling way trail continues toward Ludden Peak.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: faint fork in heather. Midground: steep forested slope. Background: Elwha valley and Hayes River country. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Ludden Peak Way Trail end (east side of Ludden Peak)
nodes.description: Where an old trail blasted into the rock simply stops on the flank of Ludden Peak. Beyond is only steep loose slope and a marked rock where the Bailey Range route begins.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: narrow ledge trail ending at loose dirt. Midground: steep scree and trees. Background: grassy saddle far below, Mount Scott beyond. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Lillian River Trail junction
nodes.description: A narrow salal-lined trail branches east up the Lillian River into old forest that few people ever see.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: signpost. Midground: salal and huge mossy trees. Background: shadowy forest. Sky: none.

nodes.name: Lillian River Trail end

camp.reservation_or_quota: Recreation.gov cross-country zone "Lillian River Trail"; camp anywhere off vegetation 200 ft from water.
camp.notes: Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain. Trail rarely maintained: blowdown, brush and a final jumble before a small riverside site.

nodes.description: The trail fades into salal, moss and fallen trunks and ends at a lonely bend of the Lillian River with one small campsite.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: mossy fallen log. Midground: small clear river over stones. Background: giant cedars. Sky: green gloom.

nodes.name: Lillian Camp (Lillian River)

camp.reservation_or_quota: Recreation.gov "Lillian River"; max group 12; not quota-limited in the Oct 2026 snapshot.
camp.notes: Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain. Fires only in established rings when no ban: Stage 2 fire restrictions (all campfires banned parkwide) were in effect from Aug 11, 2026; no lifting notice found by Oct 7, 2026. Privy; more sites across the bridge.

nodes.description: The trail switchbacks down to a bridge over the clear Lillian River, where mossy campsites sit under huge trees and the water is loud enough to sing you to sleep.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: footbridge over a rocky stream. Midground: campsites on mossy flats, privy roof. Background: towering firs. Sky: gray-green canopy light.

nodes.name: Mary's Falls Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Recreation.gov "Mary's Falls"; max group 12; not quota-limited in the Oct 2026 snapshot.
camp.notes: Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain. Fires only in established rings when no ban: Stage 2 fire restrictions (all campfires banned parkwide) were in effect from Aug 11, 2026; no lifting notice found by Oct 7, 2026. Sites are off the trail in brush with river access (WTA Aug 2026).

nodes.description: A quiet riverside camp hidden in the brush, with a small waterfall nearby and the Elwha sliding past over smooth stones.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: tent in ferns. Midground: river with gravel bar. Background: thin waterfall on a mossy cliff. Sky: blue strip.

nodes.name: Canyon Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Recreation.gov "Canyon Camp"; max group 12; not quota-limited in the Oct 2026 snapshot.
camp.notes: Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain. No toilet: bury waste. Fires only in established rings when no ban: Stage 2 fire restrictions (all campfires banned parkwide) were in effect from Aug 11, 2026; no lifting notice found by Oct 7, 2026.

nodes.description: A modest forest camp near the river where the valley narrows between steep walls.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: fire ring of stones. Midground: forest flat. Background: rock wall and river. Sky: narrow.

nodes.name: Elkhorn (camp and ranger station)

camp.reservation_or_quota: Recreation.gov "Elkhorn"; max group 12; not quota-limited in the Oct 2026 snapshot.
camp.notes: Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain. Intermittently staffed summer ranger station. Fires only in established rings when no ban: Stage 2 fire restrictions (all campfires banned parkwide) were in effect from Aug 11, 2026; no lifting notice found by Oct 7, 2026.

nodes.description: A clearing on the river with a log guard station, where a ranger may be found in summer. Elk tracks print the sandbars.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: elk tracks in sand. Midground: log ranger cabin with a flagpole. Background: river meadow and mountains. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Remann's Cabin (Dodger Point Primitive Trail junction)

camp.reservation_or_quota: Recreation.gov camp area "Remann's Cabin"; not quota-limited in the Oct 2026 snapshot.
camp.notes: Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain. Camping by the ford (WTA 2017 trip report). The Dodger Point Primitive Trail starts across the river: a ford that is only possible at low water, usually Aug-Sep.

nodes.description: An old cabin on the east bank beside a broad, cold river crossing. Across the water a faint trail starts climbing toward Dodger Point.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: gravel bar and a hiker testing the water with a pole. Midground: wide riffled river. Background: old cabin on the far bank, forested slope. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Hayes River (camp and ranger station)

camp.reservation_or_quota: Recreation.gov "Hayes River"; max group 12; not quota-limited in the Oct 2026 snapshot.
camp.notes: Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain. Intermittently staffed summer ranger station; a "great privy" (WTA Aug 2026). Fires only in rings when no ban: Stage 2 fire restrictions (all campfires banned parkwide) were in effect from Aug 11, 2026; no lifting notice found by Oct 7, 2026. Black bears feed on salmonberries here in July.

nodes.description: Where the Hayes River pours in from the east, a ranger cabin and a scatter of campsites sit in a big, salmonberry-tangled flat. It is the last comfortable stop before the climb to Hayden Pass.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: salmonberry bushes with orange berries, a bear cub peeking (optional). Midground: ranger cabin and bridge. Background: forested mountainsides. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Hayden Pass Trail junction (Hayes River bridge)
nodes.description: Across the Hayes River bridge a trail turns east and starts an eight-mile, four-thousand-foot climb to Hayden Pass and the Dosewallips.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: signpost HAYDEN PASS 8.3. Midground: steep forest. Background: hint of a burned ridge above. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Hayden Pass
nodes.description: A broad, open saddle above the scars of an old fire, with ghost trees standing silver below. On a clear day the whole range is laid out, and the trail drops away east to the meadows of the Dosewallips.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: gravel saddle and a weathered sign. Midground: slope of silver burned snags among green regrowth. Background: snowy Mount Anderson and many peaks. Sky: big clean blue.

nodes.name: Camp Wilder

camp.reservation_or_quota: Recreation.gov "Camp Wilder"; max group 12; not quota-limited in the Oct 2026 snapshot.
camp.notes: Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain. Shelter "in good repair with two bunks" plus scattered private sites (WTA Sept 2026). Toilet listing conflicts (NPS trail page: pit toilet; NPS camp map: none). Fires only in rings when no ban: Stage 2 fire restrictions (all campfires banned parkwide) were in effect from Aug 11, 2026; no lifting notice found by Oct 7, 2026.

nodes.description: A friendly camp with an old three-sided shelter and private sites scattered among logs and stumps that make fine furniture. Upstream, fire-scarred slopes begin.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: three-sided log shelter with two bunks. Midground: campsites with stump stools. Background: river and slopes of silver snags. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Chicago Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Recreation.gov "Chicago Camp"; max group 12; not quota-limited in the Oct 2026 snapshot.
camp.notes: Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain. The Elwha must be forded just beyond camp toward Low Divide; the old log is gone (NPS 8/23/26). Fires only in rings when no ban: Stage 2 fire restrictions (all campfires banned parkwide) were in effect from Aug 11, 2026; no lifting notice found by Oct 7, 2026.

nodes.description: An open, sunny camp near the head of the Elwha, where the river is small enough to wade and the peaks of the Bailey Range and Mount Christie close in on three sides.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: flat camp with a few tents. Midground: young river over cobbles. Background: steep green walls rising to snowy peaks. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Happy Hollow (shelter)

camp.reservation_or_quota: Recreation.gov camp area "Happy Hollow"; not quota-limited in the Oct 2026 snapshot.
camp.notes: Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain. Approach trail neglected for years: blowdown and brush; biting no-see-ums reported (2020 trip report).

nodes.description: An old shelter at the end of an overgrown trail, the last roof of any kind before the trackless Elwha Basin.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: collapsed-looking log shelter. Midground: overgrown trail, ferns. Background: river and steep slopes. Sky: gray.

nodes.name: Elwha Basin

camp.reservation_or_quota: Recreation.gov camp area "Elwha Basin"; not quota-limited in the Oct 2026 snapshot.
camp.water: Elwha River and side creeks; treat.
camp.notes: Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain. End of a primitive way trail; beyond is the Elwha Snowfinger route to Dodwell-Rixon Pass.

nodes.description: A wild amphitheater at the very head of the river, ringed by waterfalls pouring off cliffs, thick with brush and avalanche debris. The infant Elwha spills out of a gorge choked with old snow.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: dense green brush and a boulder. Midground: grassy basin with many white waterfall threads on cliffs. Background: narrow snow-filled gorge leading up to a pass. Sky: blue with cloud caps.

nodes.name: Lake Margaret
nodes.description: A small, still lake in the meadows just north of Low Divide, its twin Lake Mary close by. Avalanche lilies crowd the shore when the snow first melts.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: meadow flowers at the water edge. Midground: small dark lake reflecting firs. Background: Mount Christie and Mount Seattle. Sky: blue with clouds.

nodes.name: Low Divide

camp.reservation_or_quota: Owned by the North Fork Quinault region. Recreation.gov / NPS Quinault district camp.
camp.notes: Shared node; see the North Fork Quinault region for full camp details. Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain.

nodes.description: The gentle saddle between the Elwha and the Quinault, with Lakes Mary and Margaret and meadows under Mount Seattle and Mount Christie. North is the long Elwha; south, the rain forest.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: meadow with a trail sign ELWHA / QUINAULT. Midground: small lake. Background: Mount Seattle and Mount Christie. Sky: blue with clouds.

nodes.name: Appleton Pass

camp.reservation_or_quota: Shared with the Sol Duc region. Recreation.gov "Appleton Pass (No Campfires)" (Elwha district); max group 12; not quota-limited in Oct 2026.
camp.notes: Same coordinates as the Sol Duc region node (Oyster Lake trail junction just east of the crest). Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain.

nodes.description: A windy heather saddle at the top of the long Boulder Creek climb, with tiny Oyster Lake just over the crest and the Sol Duc valley dropping away beyond.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: heather and a trail sign. Midground: tiny tarn. Background: Mount Appleton and the Sol Duc valley. Sky: wind-streaked blue.

nodes.name: Cat Basin

camp.reservation_or_quota: Owned by the Sol Duc / High Divide region. Recreation.gov "Cat Basin (No Campfires)".
camp.water: Creek in the basin below the trail; treat.
camp.notes: Shared with the Sol Duc region (same id and coordinates). Start of the Bailey Range Way Trail. Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain.

nodes.description: A meadow basin at the east end of the High Divide where the last maintained trail gives way to a faint path toward the Catwalk.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: meadow with grasshoppers. Midground: basin with a creek. Background: Cat Peak. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: The Catwalk (west end)
nodes.description: The way trail ends at the brink of a knife-edged rock arm linking Cat Peak to the meadows of Mount Carrie. Beside the start is a dry, wind-scoured campsite with Mount Olympus filling the view.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: narrow rocky arete with a low point in the middle. Midground: drops on both sides into deep valleys (Hoh to the south). Background: huge white Mount Olympus. Sky: deep blue.

nodes.name: Boston Charlie's Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Bailey Range cross-country zone "Boston Charlie's (No Campfires)"; book by calling the WIC (360-565-3100).
camp.water: Small snowmelt tarn (can be foul by late summer); may be dry between here and upper Cream Lake.
camp.notes: Start of the Bailey Range traverse proper. Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain.

nodes.description: At the far end of the Catwalk a small snowmelt pond marks the old camp of a long-ago traveler. From here on there is no trail at all.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: small muddy tarn. Midground: meadow ledge. Background: the Catwalk behind and Mount Carrie ahead. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Mount Carrie camps (meadow benches, about 5,600 ft)

camp.reservation_or_quota: Bailey Range cross-country zone "Mt Carrie Sites (No Campfires)"; call the WIC.
camp.notes: Stash bear canisters in a hollow so they cannot roll down the steep slope (WTA 2005). Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain.

nodes.description: Steep meadows on the shoulder of Mount Carrie, alive with marmots and grouse, with a level spot or two for a tent and the Hoh valley yawning below.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: tent on a tiny flat, a bear canister tucked in a hollow. Midground: steep flowery meadow with a marmot. Background: Mount Olympus across the Hoh. Sky: sunset over the Pacific.

nodes.name: Mount Carrie
nodes.description: The high point of the Bailey Range, a walk-up summit with the Carrie Glacier spilling off its north side and the ocean, the Strait and Hurricane Ridge all in view.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: summit rocks. Midground: white Carrie Glacier with blue crevasses. Background: Mount Olympus and the Pacific. Sky: dark blue.

nodes.name: Carrie Glacier
nodes.description: A real glacier with real crevasses, used by some parties as a high shortcut toward Stephen Lake. Rope, harness and crevasse rescue skills are not optional here.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: roped party on snow. Midground: blue-black crevasse slots. Background: Ruth Peak. Sky: glare-white near snow.

nodes.name: Eleven Bull Basin

camp.reservation_or_quota: Bailey Range cross-country zone "11 Bull Basin (No Campfires)"; call the WIC.
camp.notes: Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain.

nodes.description: A broad basin west of Stephen Peak full of streams, waterfalls and flowers, reached by traversing high above the Hoh. Snow can hide streams under hollow bridges.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: flowers and a creek. Midground: waterfalls on benches. Background: Stephen Peak. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Stephen Lake

camp.reservation_or_quota: Bailey Range cross-country zone "Stephen Lake (No Campfires)"; call the WIC.
camp.notes: Reached by a high bypass from Eleven Bull Basin or over the Carrie Glacier. Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain.

nodes.description: A calm lake with a pebbly little beach under the comb of Stephen Peak, quieter and drier than buggy Cream Lake below.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: pebbly beach. Midground: still lake. Background: spiky ridge (Stephen's Comb). Sky: rain clouds rolling in (option).

nodes.name: Cream Lake

camp.reservation_or_quota: Bailey Range cross-country zone "Cream Lake (No Campfires)"; call the WIC.
camp.notes: Boggy meadows; mosquitoes and elk sign. Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain.

nodes.description: A milky lake in boggy meadows, crisscrossed by elk trails, where a sixteen-year-old explorer is said to have arrived in 1885. Mosquitoes rule the evenings.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: boggy meadow with elk tracks. Midground: pale cream-blue lake. Background: Mount Ferry. Sky: hazy.

nodes.name: Ferry Basin (Lake Billy Everett)

camp.reservation_or_quota: Bailey Range cross-country zone "Ferry Basin (No Campfires)"; call the WIC.
camp.water: Lakes and small streams; some lakes silty.
camp.notes: Windy at night in exposed sites. Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain.

nodes.description: A string of tarns under Mount Ferry and Mount Pulitzer, the largest named for Billy Everett, ringed with buttercups and strange shards of rock. Alpenglow paints the peaks pink at dawn.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: buttercups and sharp rock shards. Midground: chain of small lakes. Background: Mount Ferry and Mount Pulitzer glowing pink. Sky: dawn gradient.

nodes.name: Lone Tree Pass (Pulitzer Pass)

camp.reservation_or_quota: Bailey Range cross-country zone "Lone Tree Pass (No Campfires)"; call the WIC.
camp.notes: Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain.

nodes.description: A rocky gap beside Mount Ferry where the routes split: south along the range toward Bear Pass and the Elwha headwaters, or east down a ridge toward Ludden Peak and Dodger Point.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: single wind-twisted tree. Midground: rock gap. Background: two directions of peaks. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Scott-Ludden Saddle

camp.reservation_or_quota: Bailey Range cross-country zone "Scott-Ludden Saddle (No Campfires)"; call the WIC.
camp.notes: Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain.

nodes.description: A grassy saddle of stream-fed meadows between Mount Scott and Ludden Peak where elk herds pass and mountain goats sometimes graze in the trees.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: meadow stream. Midground: elk herd. Background: Ludden Peak. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Bear Pass
nodes.description: A high pass at the southern end of the range with Mount Barnes and Mount Queets ahead and the snowy wall of the Olympus massif to the west.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: talus and a boot track. Midground: meadows and snow. Background: Mount Olympus massif. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Dodwell-Rixon Pass

camp.reservation_or_quota: Bailey Range cross-country zone "Queets Basin/Dodwell-Rixon (No Campfires)"; call the WIC.
camp.water: Small lake just west of the pass; streams.
camp.notes: Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain.

nodes.description: A meadowy pass between the Queets and Elwha headwaters, with a little lake and a view of Mount Olympus. Named for two surveyors who mapped these mountains around 1900.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: pebbly lakeshore. Midground: green pass with snow patches. Background: Mount Olympus. Sky: blue.

nodes.name: Elwha Snowfinger
nodes.description: Once a long tongue of old avalanche snow filled this gorge and made an easy highway down to the basin. Now it is broken into undercut, hollow remnants over a rushing infant river, with loose scree on both sides.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: hollow snow bridge with a dark hole and water below. Midground: narrow gorge with loose scree walls. Background: green Elwha Basin far below. Sky: thin strip.

nodes.name: Queets Basin

camp.reservation_or_quota: Bailey Range cross-country zone "Queets Basin/Dodwell-Rixon (No Campfires)"; call the WIC.
camp.notes: Park-approved bear canister required for all food, garbage and scented items (parkwide rule, Recreation.gov 2026). Hanging food is prohibited even where old bear wires remain.

nodes.description: A wide green bowl at the birth of the Queets River, walled by Mount Queets and the eastern glaciers of Mount Olympus.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: meadow with braided streams. Midground: basin floor. Background: Humes Glacier and Olympus ridges. Sky: blue.

segments.notes: NPS: an additional mile on the Switchback Trail climbs ~800 ft to the ridge (DEM +810). Marmot holes in tread; a few steep side-slopes (WTA Sept 2026). segments.notes: Narrow tread blasted into rock in places across exposed cliffs and ledges (WTA). NPS GIS calls this the Switchback Trail; the park trail-conditions table counts it as part of the Lake Angeles/Klahhane Ridge Trail. Scaled with the Lake Angeles trail to NPS 6.3 mi Heart O' the Hills-to-Victor Pass. segments.notes: Steep, extremely dusty and loose descent with ankle-rolling rocks; many slips and falls reported with heavy packs (WTA Aug-Sept 2026). Recreation.gov: trail between Lake Angeles and Heather Park is steep, exposed and loose in places. DEM -1,750 ft. [Geometry 1.45 mi; Distance: NPS trail GIS geometry (Trails_Public_2019) measured with haversine; gain/loss: USGS 3DEP 10 m DEM via OpenTopoData sampled every 30 m.]

segments.snow_free_typical: June to October (NPS: generally melted out to the lake by June); lower trail most of the year
segments.notes: NPS: 3.5 mi to Lake Angeles (geometry 3.29). Footbridge over Ennis Creek; second-growth forest from a century-old fire; pond and meadow below the lake. segments.snow_free_typical: late June to early October (NPS); steep snow near the Switchback junction early season
segments.notes: Washouts and exposed sections make navigation difficult between Heather Park and the Switchback junction (NPS 6/5/26); semi-loose gravel with a few exposed spots where a fall would be long (WTA Sept 2026). Trailhead sign warns hikers have become lost here in darkness or fog. Scaled to NPS 6.2 mi trail total. [Geometry 1.53 mi; Distance: NPS trail GIS geometry (Trails_Public_2019) measured with haversine; gain/loss: USGS 3DEP 10 m DEM via OpenTopoData sampled every 30 m.]

segments.snow_free_typical: late June to early October above ~4,000 ft
segments.notes: Long switchbacking descent flanking First Top; no water between Heather Park and the trailhead. [Geometry 2.6 mi; Distance: NPS trail GIS geometry (Trails_Public_2019) measured with haversine; gain/loss: USGS 3DEP 10 m DEM via OpenTopoData sampled every 30 m.]

segments.snow_free_typical: usually snow-free most of the year below ~2,000 ft; occasional winter snow and blowdown after storms
segments.notes: Steady climb through second-growth hemlock with Alaska cedar higher up. Halfway Rock is a glacial erratic just off the trail. [Geometry 1.65 mi; Distance: NPS trail GIS geometry (Trails_Public_2019) measured with haversine; gain/loss: USGS 3DEP 10 m DEM via OpenTopoData sampled every 30 m.]

segments.snow_free_typical: August-September best; rotten snow in the gullies into July/August
segments.notes: Climbers' path leaves the Klahhane Ridge Trail about 2.5 mi from the visitor center (slightly west of this junction), climbs meadow and subalpine forest to a scree slope, then class 3 scrambling to the 6,454-ft summit. WTA round trip from the visitor center: 6.25 mi, 2,100 ft gain, implying roughly 0.6 mi from the trail fork (derived, not measured). Experienced scramblers only.

segments.snow_free_typical: Hurricane Hill Road open summer (opened 7/3/26); closed with winter snow
segments.notes: Hurricane Hill Road beyond the visitor center (1.5 mi total, narrow, not for RVs). Picnic areas A and B are about one mile beyond the main parking area (NPS brochure). Normally driven; gain/loss are endpoint DEM differences only.
End of Hurricane Hill Road (NPS: 1.5 mi from the Hurricane Ridge parking area). Normally driven. Endpoint DEM values only.

segments.snow_free_typical: late June/early July to October; snow can linger into July
segments.notes: Paved, about 8 ft wide; first ~2,700 ft under 5% grade (WTA). No toilet at the trailhead; restrooms ~0.3 mi back down the road (2026 report). High variant used by some parties (BCP: "Carrie moraine" to "Ruth col"), roped for crevasses on the north side of the moraine/berm.

Over a steep col with a very steep, loose descent snowfield into the Stephen Lake basin. BCP day total Sol Duc Park-Catwalk-Mount Carrie-Carrie moraine-Ruth col-Stephen Lake basin: 7.64 mi, +5,138 ft, ~14 hours.

Bailey Range cross-country route: no trail, no signs; ice axe, crampons/microspikes and route-finding required; bear canister required; permits by phone with the WIC. Path rises a few hundred feet then descends ~1,000 ft through trees into the wet meadows of Cream Lake Basin (WTA 2005).
High bypass: before the descent to Cream Lake, climb a steep meadow north to a low point on the ridge, then around to Stephen Lake (2020 report).

Bailey Range cross-country route: no trail, no signs; ice axe, crampons/microspikes and route-finding required; bear canister required; permits by phone with the WIC. Around the north side of Cream Lake through boggy meadows, then scramble up a creek bed into Ferry Basin (WTA 2005).

Bailey Range cross-country route: no trail, no signs; ice axe, crampons/microspikes and route-finding required; bear canister required; permits by phone with the WIC. Ledge and cliff-band maze down to the basin floor, ford of the braided Stephen Lake outlet (2-3 ft deep), class 3-4 moves up steep heather, traverse of Stephen Peak and a brushy "second catwalk" with nasty gully crossings. Mileage and gain are one party's GPS day total (BCP).
Past a lake ringed by rock and snow and another at the foot of a small glacier (~5,500 ft) to Pulitzer (Lone Tree) Pass at 5,720 ft; Mount Ferry summit ~20 min above (WTA 2005).

Bailey Range cross-country route: no trail, no signs; ice axe, crampons/microspikes and route-finding required; bear canister required; permits by phone with the WIC. Loose scree (helmets), a traverse of the Childs Glacier at ~5,600 ft (firm morning snow: axe/spikes), a jumbled talus basin, then a ridge south to Bear Pass (2020 report). BCP day total Ferry Basin-Mount Pulitzer-Lone Tree Pass-Bear Pass: 5.13 mi, +2,806 ft.

Short exit: go back up nearly to Mount Ferry, descend east onto the ridge toward Ludden Peak (cliffs block the direct line), then a winding path above Long Creek and a few hundred feet down to the 4,700-ft saddle (WTA 2005).
Descend south past meadow streams to the small lake just west of Dodwell-Rixon Pass (2020 report). Straight-line ~1.0 mi.
