hazards.name: The washed-out Elwha road: 6.5 to 8 extra miles before the trail
hazards.real_world: Olympic Hot Springs Road has been closed to vehicles at Madison Falls since the river took out a section of road; hikers detour on a 0.8-mi bypass trail and walk or bike 6.5 mi to Whiskey Bend or ~8 mi to Boulder Creek. Trees lie across the road, Whiskey Bend Road has washed-out dips, and bikes are not allowed past the trailheads.
hazards.game_event_idea: At the gate: (A) Walk it with the full pack: +6.5 mi, arrive tired (-1 energy) but 100% reliable. (B) Ride a bike with the pack: 80% arrive fresh and early / 15% walk the bike through the bypass and lose time / 5% crash in a washed-out dip on the way back (scrapes, -1 morale). Bike lock in pack +10% (bike still there on return); e-bike: +speed but 20% stuck lifting it over logs. (C) Choose another trailhead instead. (Percentages are suggested game-design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Elwha River ford beyond Chicago Camp
hazards.season: dangerous in snowmelt (May-early July) and after heavy rain; ankle-deep in a dry September
hazards.real_world: The trail toward Low Divide crosses the Elwha just past Chicago Camp. The big log that used to span it is gone, so it must be forded (NPS, Aug 2026). It was ankle-deep in early Sept 2026; in high water it can be impassable.
hazards.game_event_idea: River runs (roll weather): low / medium / high. (A) Wade now: low 98% fine, 2% soaked boots; medium 80% fine, 15% soaked and cold (-1 warmth), 5% swept and lose an item; high 50% fine, 35% soaked, 15% fall in (hypothermia check, trip may end with a ranger assist). (B) Wait until early morning when snowmelt drops: +30% to the next roll, costs half a day. (C) Turn back to Hayes River. Water shoes +10%, poles +15%, unbuckled hip belt reduces item loss. (Percentages are suggested game-design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Elwha ford at Remann's Cabin (Dodger Point Primitive Trail)
hazards.season: NPS: impossible in fall, winter, spring and early summer; possible only at low water, usually August-September
hazards.real_world: The Dodger Point Primitive Trail can only be reached from the Elwha River Trail by fording the main Elwha at Remann's Cabin. A 2017 hiker crossed at ~400 cfs and turned back at ~1,000 cfs when the water was murky and thigh-deep.
hazards.game_event_idea: Standing on the gravel bar: (A) Cross: if river < "low": 85% safe, 15% soaked; if "medium": 50% safe / 35% turn back mid-river / 15% fall in (lose food bag, trip ends early). (B) Wait a day: river drops one level 60% of the time unless it rains. (C) Give up and walk around via the Elwha trail. A friend with you: +10%. (Percentages are suggested game-design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Hayes Fire burn and the exposed slide below Hayden Pass
hazards.real_world: The upper ~3 mi of the Hayden Pass Trail cross the 2016 Hayes Fire: no shade, standing dead snags, rough tread dug up by marmots, and 135+ downed trees in 2025 (cleared by a crew in 2026). Just west of the pass an eroded, exposed dirt slide is narrow with a high-consequence fall.
hazards.game_event_idea: Afternoon heat in the burn: (A) Push on: 60% fine, 30% overheated (-1 energy, need +1 L water), 10% slip on the slide (sprain; limp to Dose Meadows). (B) Rest in the last shade and climb at dawn: 95% fine but uses a day. (C) Retreat to Hayes River. Sun hat, extra water capacity, poles each +10%. Wind gusts: 5% a snag falls nearby (story beat, no injury in the default mode). (Percentages are suggested game-design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Loose, dusty descents and exposure around Klahhane Ridge
hazards.real_world: 2026 hikers describe the drop from Klahhane Ridge to Lake Angeles as extremely steep, dusty and loose, with repeated falls; the Heather Park side has semi-loose gravel, washouts and exposed spots, and the park warns hikers have become lost there in fog or darkness.
hazards.game_event_idea: Top of the dusty chute with a heavy pack: (A) Go slow with poles: 90% fine. (B) Go fast to beat the dark: 70% fine / 25% slide and scrape (-1 health) / 5% twisted ankle (hobble to the lake; next day short). (C) Take the long way around via Hurricane Ridge and the shuttle. Lighter pack (-20% weight) +10%; boots vs trail runners +5%. (Percentages are suggested game-design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Wind, fog, lightning and snow on the high ridges
hazards.season: any month; thunderstorms July-August; first snows late September
hazards.real_world: Hurricane Ridge is named for gales over 75 mph and gets 30-35 ft of snow a year; snow can fall any month. Late September 2026 brought snow showers, howling wind and sub-30 F nights at Appleton Pass; fog regularly swallows Klahhane Ridge.
hazards.game_event_idea: Clouds boil up the valley at 2 pm: (A) Keep going to the pass: 65% clears, 25% whiteout (navigation check: map+compass or GPS or lose an hour), 10% thunder (must retreat; scary story beat). (B) Wait it out below treeline: 85% safe, lose time. (C) Turn back. Rain shell and warm layer prevent the "cold and wet" penalty; tent with a good fly prevents a sleepless night. (Percentages are suggested game-design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Steep early-season snow on Grand Valley, Lake Angeles and Appleton trails
hazards.season: June to mid-July in a normal year (2026 was a low-snow year)
hazards.real_world: NPS: several steep snow slopes exist on the Grand Valley and Lake Angeles/Heather Park trails in early season; an ice axe and self-arrest skills may be required, and the trail may be hard to follow. A high-angle snowfield lingers late just east of the Obstruction Point lot.
hazards.game_event_idea: A slanting snowfield blocks the trail: (A) Kick steps across: 70% fine / 25% slip and slide to a stop (-1 health) / 5% long slide into rocks (trip ends; ranger assist in gentle mode). Ice axe +20%, microspikes +15%, poles +5%. (B) Wait for the sun to soften it: +20% but afternoon storms roll. (C) Find a way around through rocks: 50% works, 50% dead end. (Percentages are suggested game-design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Black bears and food storage
hazards.real_world: Bear canisters are required everywhere in the Olympic wilderness. NPS reported a potentially habituated bear around Boulder Creek camp (2026); hikers saw four bears on one July 2026 Elwha trip and "chatty bears" near Humes Ranch; a bear fed on salmonberries at Hayes River. Old bear wires at Boulder Creek were being decommissioned in Sept 2026.
hazards.game_event_idea: Night noise at camp: (A) Canister locked 30 m away: 95% the bear sniffs and leaves (sketch it in the journal at dawn), 5% it bats the canister into the brush (search for it in the morning, lose an hour). (B) Food in the tent or a hang: 60% bear gets food (trip ends early, ranger lecture, -score) / 40% lucky. (C) Bang pots and shout: +10% to scare it if food is secure. Forgot the canister: the ranger at the Port Angeles WIC lends one free (store step reminder). (Percentages are suggested game-design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Cougars in the Elwha valley
hazards.real_world: The Elwha has an established cougar population: a youth group saw one at Humes Ranch, big-cat scat was found near Whiskey Bend, and Long Ridge had "tons of cougar scat" (2026 reports). Attacks are rare.
hazards.game_event_idea: A tawny shape on the trail ahead: (A) Make yourself big, stay together, back away slowly: 97% it melts into the forest, 3% it lingers and you wait it out (lose an hour). (B) Run: 70% fine / 30% it follows and you must face it (default mode: it leaves; death mode: danger). (C) Kneel to photograph it: big score for the sketchbook, small risk. Hiking with companions makes encounters rarer. (Percentages are suggested game-design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Food-stealing deer, chipmunks and marmot burrows
hazards.real_world: Grand Valley deer try to steal snacks from packs and lick urine for salt; chipmunks swarmed a car at Obstruction Point because of food smells; marmot burrows on the Badger Valley trail are ankle-breakers.
hazards.game_event_idea: Lunch break at Grand Lake: (A) Pack left open: 40% a deer steals a snack bag (lose 1 food). (B) Everything zipped: 100% safe. Later on Badger Valley: 10% stumble into a burrow (minor sprain) unless using poles (5%). (Percentages are suggested game-design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Dry ridges: Long Ridge, Lillian Ridge, Happy Lake Ridge, Dodger Point
hazards.real_world: Long Ridge has almost no water (last reliable water ~3.5 mi below the lookout spur in Aug 2026) and Recreation.gov says Dodger Point camp has none; Lillian Ridge and Grand Ridge have none; much of Happy Lake Ridge is dry; Heather Park's creek is the only water on that trail.
hazards.game_event_idea: Halfway up a sunny ridge with one bottle left: (A) Ration and continue: 60% fine / 40% dehydrated (-1 energy, slower). (B) Detour to a mapped tarn: 70% water, 30% dry. (C) Turn back to the last stream. Packing 3+ L capacity and a filter makes this event mostly harmless. (Percentages are suggested game-design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Olympic Hot Springs: bacteria and scalding pools
hazards.real_world: The pools are not monitored and may contain high levels of fecal coliform; some are very hot (WTA cites up to 118 F); nudity is common; campfires are banned year-round in the area.
hazards.game_event_idea: Steam drifts from the pools: (A) Soak in a warm-not-hot pool with your head up: 85% blissful (+2 morale), 15% upset stomach tomorrow. (B) Dunk your head: 40% sick. (C) Just sketch the steam and ferns (+journal page). Testing temperature with a hand first prevents a scald event. (Percentages are suggested game-design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Bailey Range: arete, glaciers, crevasses, and the broken Elwha Snowfinger
hazards.season: late July-mid September; snow bridges weaken through the season
hazards.real_world: The traverse crosses the exposed Catwalk, the Childs Glacier (axe/spikes) and for some parties the crevassed Carrie Glacier (roped). The Elwha Snowfinger, once continuous, is now broken into hollow, undercut remnants above a rushing river, followed by a brutal brush maze into Elwha Basin. Parties report 14-hour days and class 3-4 moves.
hazards.game_event_idea: At the top of the snowfinger: (A) Walk the snow: 60% fast and fine / 30% punch through to the knee (-1 health) / 10% snow bridge collapses (rescue scenario; death possible only in "Sierra" mode). Ice axe +15%, roped team +15%. (B) Scramble the loose scree beside it: 75% fine / 25% rockfall scare. (C) Retreat over Dodwell-Rixon to the Queets side or back north (adds 2 days; requires food reserve). (Percentages are suggested game-design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Cross-country "shortcuts" off the trail
hazards.real_world: Steep forested and cliffy slopes hide drop-offs. In September 2026 a solo hiker attempting a cross-country traverse from Boulder Lake to Appleton Pass was found deceased on the northwest slope of Mount Appleton. A 2025 hiker on the Ludden Peak descent slid 10-15 ft on loose rock and took two hours to descend 800 ft.
hazards.game_event_idea: The map shows a short line between two trails: (A) Take the shortcut alone: 40% saves time / 40% cliffed out, backtrack (lose half a day) / 20% fall (default mode: rescue and trip ends; Sierra mode: game over). (B) With a partner, map, compass and a turnaround time: 70% / 25% / 5%. (C) Stay on the trail: 100% safe, +2 hours. Leaving an itinerary with someone at home makes rescues faster. (Percentages are suggested game-design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Lightning fires, smoke and campfire bans
hazards.real_world: Stage 2 restrictions banned all campfires parkwide from Aug 11, 2026. A 0.5-acre lightning fire burned ~1.5 mi SE of Mount Barnes in Aug 2026 (rappelers cut line; no closures). The 2023 lightning fires (Delabarre, 4,088 acres) closed the upper Elwha that year; fire-damaged areas between Hayes River and Chicago Camp still drop trees and rocks.
hazards.game_event_idea: Smoke smudges the sky: (A) Continue: 80% just hazy views, 20% a ranger reroutes you (closure) and the trip shortens. (B) Plan a campfire dinner: if a ban is on, the meal plan fails (must have a stove) and a ranger may cite you. Packing a stove makes bans irrelevant. (Percentages are suggested game-design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Blowdown, brush and a landslide-undercut tread in the upper Elwha
hazards.season: all season; worst early summer before crews
hazards.real_world: NPS (Aug 23, 2026): 45 trees down between Hayes River and Chicago Camp with very brushy sections; ~0.5 mi south of the Hayes River junction a 20-ft section of trail is undercut by a landslide; Low Divide-Chicago overgrown and hard to follow.
hazards.game_event_idea: A jackstraw of logs: (A) Climb over with the full pack: 85% fine / 15% scraped shin and torn pants (-1 morale). (B) Go around through brush: 70% fine / 30% lose the trail for an hour. At the undercut section: walk lightly one at a time (safe) vs. hurry together (10% edge crumbles: drop an item). (Percentages are suggested game-design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Cold rain and early-season or fall cold snaps
hazards.real_world: On Sept 25-26, 2026 a Mountaineers party at Appleton Pass endured rain, snow showers, howling wind and temperatures below 30 F with wet clothes and struggled to stay warm.
hazards.game_event_idea: Camp at the pass in sleet: (A) Pitch fast, change into dry clothes, hot drink: fine if you packed a warm bag and dry layers. (B) No dry layer: 50% shivering night (-2 energy), 10% hypothermia (descend at dawn; trip ends). (C) Drop below treeline before camping: safer, but a longer day. (Percentages are suggested game-design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Crowds, parking and permits on the Hurricane Ridge side
hazards.real_world: Lake Angeles and Hurricane Hill lots fill early on weekends; Lake Angeles camp is very busy; Grand Valley is a quota area (Jul 1 - Oct 15 reservation season); rangers check permits and canisters.
hazards.game_event_idea: Planning screen: (A) Reserve on April 15 when reservations open: 90% you get your first choice. (B) Try a week before: 40% first choice, 40% second, 20% nothing (pick a non-quota camp like Humes Ranch). Trailhead at 10 am Saturday: 60% no parking (take the shuttle or walk the road). (Percentages are suggested game-design odds, not real-world statistics.)

hazards.name: Missing footlogs and sketchy log bridges on Boulder Creek
hazards.season: worst in snowmelt and after rain
hazards.real_world: The North Fork Boulder Creek footlog has washed away (ford on rolling rocks); Crystal Creek is crossed on a sketchy single-log bridge; a bridge above upper Boulder Creek falls was damaged but passable (2026).
hazards.game_event_idea: A single wet log over a loud creek: (A) Walk it upright: 75% fine / 20% wobble and drop a trekking pole / 5% fall in (soaked, -1 warmth). (B) Scoot across seated: 95% fine, slow and undignified (+1 humility). (C) Wade below: depends on water level. (Percentages are suggested game-design odds, not real-world statistics.)

wildlife_and_plants.name: Olympic marmot
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Found only on the Olympic Peninsula; Washington's official endemic mammal. Cat-sized, whistles warnings, hibernates from about September to May. Burrows riddle Badger Valley and the Hayden Pass burn.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Helper character who whistles a warning before storms or snowfields; sketch for the journal; burrow is also a minor trip hazard.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Columbian black-tailed deer
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Very bold around Hurricane Ridge and Grand Valley; will steal food and lick urine for salt (NPS asks hikers to urinate on rocks or trail).
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Comic food-thief encounter; teaches pack discipline.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Black bear
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Common; a potentially habituated bear reported at Boulder Creek (NPS 2026). Feeds on salmonberries, huckleberries and blueberries in summer.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: In homage to the picture book, a calm bear can be a wise advisor seen at a distance who "points" toward the berries (never feed or approach). Bear-canister check event.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Cougar (mountain lion)
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Established population in the Elwha; frequent sign and some sightings in 2026.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Rare tense encounter; rewards the "stay together, look big" choice.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Roosevelt elk
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Herds in the upper Elwha and Bailey Range meadows; the 1952 Disney film "The Olympic Elk" was shot partly from Humes Ranch.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Distant herd crossing a meadow at dawn; an elk bugle in September; Elkhorn place-name lore.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Mountain goat
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Non-native (introduced in the 1920s). 381 were removed from the Olympics in 2018-2020 (325 moved to the Cascades); a few remain in remote areas. A rutting billy fatally gored a hiker near Klahhane Ridge in October 2010.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Rare sighting in the Bailey Range; story note that the park moved goats to the Cascades; never approach.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Salmon (Chinook, coho, steelhead) returning to the Elwha
wildlife_and_plants.notes: After the Elwha (1913) and Glines Canyon (1927) dams were removed in 2011-2014, salmon spawned in the park within months. Fishing in the Elwha and tributaries is closed.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Late-summer journal page: red-sided fish holding below Goblins Gate; restoration story told by a ranger at Glines Canyon.

wildlife_and_plants.name: American dipper
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Gray songbird that walks underwater in fast creeks; noted patrolling the creek in the Bailey Range (WTA 2005).
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Cheerful companion at river camps; sketchable.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Sooty grouse
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Hens with chicks along the Hurricane Hill trail in July 2026; also seen in Bailey Range meadows.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Mother grouse leads chicks across the path: wait (+morale) or rush (-score).

wildlife_and_plants.name: Common raven
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Rides the ridge winds; notorious for opening unattended packs.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Trickster helper or thief; tells you a storm is coming by tumbling in the wind.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Mountain bluebird
wildlife_and_plants.notes: A small flock seen on Klahhane Ridge in Sept 2026.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Rare bright-blue sketch for the journal (EGA light blue).

wildlife_and_plants.name: Glacier lily (yellow avalanche/glacier lily, Erythronium grandiflorum)
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Golden-yellow lilies that bloom right at the edge of melting snow on high meadows in early summer.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Strong candidate for the in-game "golden glow" homage: a golden flower found at the edge of the snow near a summit, to be sketched, not picked (picking plants is prohibited in the park).

wildlife_and_plants.name: Olympic Mountain groundsel (Senecio neowebsteri)
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Rare yellow-flowered daisy endemic to high scree in the Olympic Mountains.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Rare high-scree "golden" find for expert routes; journal bonus.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Piper's bellflower (Olympic harebell, Campanula piperi)
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Endemic to the Olympics; blue-violet flowers growing from rock crevices; a 2026 hiker spotted them on Klahhane Ridge.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Rock-crevice sketch target; teaches "look, don't pick".

wildlife_and_plants.name: Flett's violet (Olympic violet, Viola flettii)
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Pink-violet violet endemic to rocky outcrops and talus of the northeastern and eastern Olympics, ~4,400-6,600 ft; photographed in bloom on Hurricane Ridge.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Field-guide page with "only found here" stamp.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Olympic Mountain synthyris (Synthyris pinnatifida var. lanuginosa)
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Rare woolly-leaved alpine plant of gravelly summits in the Olympics (NPS lists it as endemic and rare); historically threatened by mountain goats.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Rare summit-gravel find; links to the goat story.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Subalpine fir
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Narrow spire-shaped fir of the drier northeast Olympics; clones itself by layering lower branches under the snowpack, forming tree islands.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Signature EGA silhouette (dark green spires) for all Hurricane Ridge scenes; field-guide tree page.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Pacific madrone
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Red-barked broadleaf evergreen on sunny, dry, rocky slopes of the lower Elwha.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Peeling red bark sketch; marks a hot, dry trail stretch (drink water).

wildlife_and_plants.name: Old-growth Douglas-fir, western redcedar and western hemlock
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Huge trees along the Elwha and Lillian rivers; bigleaf maples draped in moss in the valley bottoms.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Field-guide spread of trees (homage to the book's tree pages).

wildlife_and_plants.name: Salmonberry, huckleberry and blueberry
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Berries ripen July-September; bears feed heavily on them.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Forage a handful (+morale) but watch for bears doing the same.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Beard lichen
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Pale green "old man's beard" drapes the second-growth trees on the Heather Park trail.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Dithered pale-green texture in forest scenes; journal entry.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Fly agaric (Amanita muscaria)
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Red-capped, white-spotted toadstools common around PJ Lake in late summer (poisonous).
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Storybook toadstool sketch; never eat.

permit_and_rules.rule: A wilderness permit is required for every overnight stay in the park wilderness, year-round, reserved in advance on Recreation.gov (no trailhead self-registration). The WIC issues it 3 days before the trip and you print it yourself.

Fees: $6 non-refundable reservation fee per permit + $8 per person per night (16 and older); 15 and under free but count toward group size; $45 Annual Wilderness Pass covers the nightly fee for the holder. Park entrance fee/pass is separate.
Summer-season (May 15 - Oct 15) reservations opened April 15, 2026 at 7 am PDT; winter-season (Oct 16 - May 14) reservations opened Sept 15, 2026.

Grand Valley is a quota area: reservation season Jul 1 - Oct 15 (2026); camp only at designated sites (Grand Lake, Moose Lake, Gladys Lake); itinerary changes must be made on Recreation.gov or at a WIC before the trip. Oct 2026 nightly quotas: Grand Lake 7 groups/20 people, Moose Lake 6/22 plus a 7-12 group site, Gladys Lake 4/10. Badger Valley, Grand Pass and Lake Lillian camp zones showed 0 availability.

Groups of 7-12 in Grand Valley must use the Moose Lake group site; most Grand Valley and Dodger Point camps cap groups at 6. Parkwide max group 12 people and 8 stock; affiliated groups must camp and travel at least 1 mile apart.

All food, garbage and scented items must be stored in a park-approved bear canister for every overnight stay in the wilderness; hanging food (bear wires or self-made hangs) is prohibited. Canisters are lent free at the Port Angeles WIC.

Campfires are prohibited above 3,500 ft (all Hurricane Ridge, Grand Valley, Heather Park, Lake Angeles, Boulder Lake, Appleton, Dodger Point and Bailey Range camps) and year-round at Olympic Hot Springs / Boulder Creek. Below 3,500 ft (Elwha valley camps) fires only in established rings with dead and down wood and only when no ban is in effect.

Stage 2 fire restrictions from Aug 11, 2026: all campfires prohibited in Olympic National Park and Olympic National Forest; gas stoves allowed 3 ft from vegetation. No lifting notice found by Oct 7, 2026.

Bear-canister rule plus camp-specific maximum group sizes appear on each Recreation.gov camp area; Bailey Range and other cross-country zones (Boston Charlie's, Mt Carrie Sites, 11 Bull Basin, Stephen Lake, Cream Lake, Ferry Basin, Scott-Ludden Saddle, Lone Tree Pass, Queets Basin/Dodwell-Rixon) are booked by contacting the WIC at 360-565-3100.

Pets and bicycles are not allowed on park trails. On the closed Olympic Hot Springs and Whiskey Bend roads and the washout bypass trail, pedestrians, bicycles, stock and leashed pets are allowed; bikes must be left at the Whiskey Bend and Boulder Creek trailheads.
The Elwha River and its tributaries are closed to fishing. Fishing is allowed (no license needed in the park) at Boulder Lake (non-native brook trout) and other lakes subject to park regulations.

Use toilets where provided (Grand Lake and Moose Lake composting toilets; pit toilets at Lillian, Mary's Falls, Elkhorn, Hayes River, Camp Wilder, Chicago Camp, Boulder Creek and Boulder Lake). Elsewhere bury waste 6-8 in deep and 200 ft (70 steps) from water, trails and camps; pack out toilet paper.

Stock: day-use only in Grand Valley, Lake Angeles, Heather Park, Appleton Pass and Boulder Lake; prohibited on the Elwha to Hurricane Hill trail; Wolf Creek not stock-passable to Whiskey Bend; Little River not stock-passable (2026).
No overnight camping in the Hurricane Ridge parking lots; Hurricane Ridge Road in winter is open Fri-Sun and holiday Mondays (weather permitting) and all vehicles must carry chains.
Cancellation: 3+ full days before the start date for a refund (the $6 fee is non-refundable). Once issued, a permit cannot be changed without WIC approval. Camp only in the camp area on your permit.

Winter (Oct 16 - May 14): Recreation.gov offers winter-only snow-camping zones along the closed Hurricane Hill Road and Obstruction Point Road; a wilderness permit is still required, and Hurricane Ridge Road is open only Fri-Sun and holidays in winter.
Grand Valley designated-site counts used here equal the October 2026 nightly group quotas (Grand Lake 7, Moose Lake 6 + 1 group site, Gladys Lake 4); PJ Lake has two sites per WTA.
Do not pick plants or disturb wildlife; urinate on rock or trail so deer and goats do not dig up plants for salt.

conditions_2026.note: Olympic Hot Springs Road closed to vehicles at the Madison Falls parking area (washout); open to pedestrians, bikes, stock and leashed pets; toilet open at Madison Falls; no facilities beyond the gate. Whiskey Bend Road also closed to vehicles.
Walk-in distances: +6.5 mi to Whiskey Bend and ~8 mi to Boulder Creek (NPS trail conditions); other NPS pages say +7 mi to Whiskey Bend and 7.9 mi to Boulder Creek.

Hurricane Ridge Road open; Hurricane Hill Road open; Obstruction Point Road open (not for RVs, trailers or buses); Heart O' the Hills campground open; Hurricane Ridge staffed intermittently with limited services.

2026 Hurricane Ridge construction: water system and utility replacement; work in the main parking lot; portable restrooms and temporary water as needed; no potable water on Hurricane Ridge; possible rolling closures. Restrooms on Hurricane Hill Road under construction in July.

Hurricane Ridge Day Lodge (burned May 7, 2023): replacement in design; architect contracted Sept 19, 2025; geotechnical surveys Oct 15, 2025; construction no earlier than 2028 and likely 2-3 seasons. No indoor facilities, food or gift shop today.
Senator Murray said in May 2026 the lodge rebuild remains a priority; $80M was secured in a 2024 disaster supplemental; design/proposals planned 2027, contract start 2028.

Elwha River Trail cleared of downed trees to Hayes River Camp; 45 trees down between Hayes River and Chicago Camp with very brushy sections; fire-damaged areas between Hayes River and Chicago Camp (falling trees, loose rock, ash); a 20-ft section ~0.5 mi south of the Hayes River junction undercut by a landslide.

Elwha ford south of Chicago Camp no longer has a downed tree across it and must be forded; Low Divide-Chicago Camp stretch overgrown and hard to follow in places. A hiker found the ford ankle-deep in early September.

Hayden Pass Trail: eroded, exposed section west of the pass; many blowdowns from the 2016 Hayes Fire (NPS 7/11/26). A crew then cleared the Elwha side up to the pass (WTA trip report Aug 16, 2026); lower 5 mi described as immaculate in early September.

Boulder Creek / Olympic Hot Springs: year-round burn ban; reports of a potentially habituated bear around the camp; several large trees across the road (bikers dismount); bikes not allowed beyond the trailhead.
Boulder Creek camp bear-hang cables being decommissioned; bring a canister (free loan at the Port Angeles WIC).

Madison Falls trailhead and Glines Canyon overlook toilets found locked (overlook toilet window broken) in June 2026; NPS lists the Madison Falls toilet as open in October. Crystal Creek crossed on a sketchy single-log bridge.
Long Ridge Trail cleared of downed trees (NPS 6/14/26; volunteer crew removed 171 logs in July 2025). Water scarce: last water ~3.5 mi below the Dodger Point spur in mid-August 2026.
Geyser Valley trail (Goblins Gate to Humes Ranch): crumbling, flooded boggy bridges and overgrown trail.

Klahhane Ridge/Switchback trails in good condition with marmot holes; patchy snow on Klahhane Ridge as of 05/29/26; trail to Lake Angeles very dry, dusty and loose in August; heavy wildfire smoke days in August.
Little River Trail: many downed trees removed 4/14/26 with some remaining; slide 0.5 mi past the first foot-log dangerous for stock.
Elwha to Hurricane Hill Trail: bottom 3 mi very brushy; not stock-passable.
Stage 2 fire restrictions: all campfires prohibited parkwide from Aug 11, 2026 (reaffirmed Aug 26); no lifting notice found by Oct 7, 2026.

Mt. Barnes Fire: lightning-caused, 0.5 acre of high-elevation forest ~1.5 mi SE of the Mt. Barnes summit (upper Elwha / Bailey Range south end), reported by backpackers Aug 14, 2026; rappelers cut line; no closures.
A solo hiker who left Madison Falls Aug 31, 2026 planning a cross-country traverse from Boulder Lake to Appleton Pass was found deceased on the northwest slope of Mount Appleton on Sept 13, 2026.
Hurricane Ridge Road was closed on a Sunday morning in early August 2026 for a bike race (permit holders were emailed).

Clallam Transit seasonal Hurricane Ridge shuttle ran in 2026 (Gateway Transit Center - Lake Angeles TH - Switchback TH - Hurricane Ridge; $1, cash; park entry pass required); a Sept 6, 2026 schedule still listed it on Sundays. End-of-season date not found.
Grand Valley camps busy but available on weekdays; habituated deer and chipmunks; Obstruction Point toilet stocked (Aug 2026); dogs seen illegally at Grand Lake.

Oct 7, 2026 Recreation.gov snapshot: all Elwha-district camps showed effectively unlimited online availability (non-quota); Grand Valley quotas as listed under permits; Badger Valley, Grand Pass, Lake Lillian zones 0.

Elwha and Whiskey Bend road statuses in the NPS road table carry a 5/7/21 date (closure record); the reroute studied in the 2019 Olympic Hot Springs Road Long-Term Access EA has not been built and no decision or schedule was found (possibly stale planning info).

uncertain_claims: Segment miles are NPS GIS trail geometry (Trails_Public_2019, partly GPS-mapped in the late 1990s) scaled per trail to NPS published lengths where those exist: Elwha River Trail x1.039 to 28.4 mi Whiskey Bend-Low Divide (NPS conditions table instead says 27.7 mi to Lake Margaret), Lake Angeles 3.5 mi to the lake and 6.3 mi to Victor Pass, Heather Park 6.2 mi (NPS page says 6.3), Switchback 1.6, Hayden Pass 8.3 (geometry 7.61), Appleton (Boulder side) 7.7, Happy Lake Ridge 9.5, Little River 6.8, PJ Lake 0.9, Long Ridge 10.5, Dodger Point primitive 5.3. Sub-segment splits are proportional, not signed mileages.
Elwha mileposts disagree among sources: Elkhorn 11-11.5 (this file 11.7), Hayes River 16.1 (Backpacker) vs 16.9 here; a 2026 hiker estimated "about 15" to Hayes River.

Grand Valley distances left unscaled (NPS 3.7 mi to Grand Lake matches the geometry), but the NPS conditions table gives 7.7 mi Obstruction Point-Cameron Creek junction vs 7.3 by geometry; Badger Valley NPS 4.7 mi vs 4.4 geometry vs WTA 4.1.

Madison Falls-Whiskey Bend road walk: NPS says 6.5 mi (trail conditions) and 7 mi (Elwha River Trail page); WTA 6.2; a cyclist measured Whiskey Bend Road at 4.4 vs the 5-mi sign. This file uses 2.2 + 4.3 = 6.5.

Madison Falls-Boulder Creek Trailhead: NPS ~8 / 7.9 mi; WTA 8; Recreation.gov 8; this file 8.2 from OSM road geometry. Recreation.gov says 8 mi to the Happy Lake Ridge Trailhead, but OSM geometry places it ~6.8 mi from Madison Falls.
Road-walk gains for the washout bypass are understated (OSM road line bridged straight across the washout).
Hurricane Hill Road segments (1.0 + 0.5 mi) use NPS brochure figures; their gain/loss are endpoint DEM differences only.

Lillian Ridge Way Trail is not in the NPS GIS layer; distance (2.3 mi) is from a single OpenStreetMap way plus a 0.2-mi connector to the NPS Grand Pass Trail line; its exact junction location south of Gladys Lake is approximate.
Lillian River Trail length: NPS page 2.3 mi, NPS GIS 2.54 (label "mile 3.0"), WTA 2.5.
Toilet presence conflicts between the NPS camp KML, Recreation.gov text and NPS trail pages at Humes Ranch, Camp Wilder, Lake Angeles, Heather Park and Appleton Pass (set to null where conflicting).

Food storage: the NPS camp KML still lists "Bear Wire" at many Elwha camps, but Recreation.gov 2026 rules require canisters everywhere and prohibit hanging; Recreation.gov text for Appleton Pass still says "use available bear wire or bear canisters". Game default: canister required.
Fires: whether the Aug 11, 2026 Stage 2 campfire ban had been lifted by Oct 7, 2026 could not be confirmed.
Dodger Point camp water: Recreation.gov says no water; trip reports describe a small stream crossing the path to the campground and tarns below the point, low by midsummer.

The location of the Elwha ford relative to Chicago Camp is described inconsistently ("at Chicago Camp", "south of Chicago Camp", "between Chicago and Wilder"); modeled on the Chicago Camp-Lake Margaret segment (the Low Divide approach).

Long Ridge Trail Elwha crossing ("Dodger Point Bridge") is placed ~0.1 mi from the Humes Ranch loop junction from the geometry; 2026 bridge condition not explicitly confirmed (trail reported in use and cleared).

Ludden Peak Way Trail: NPS GIS shows only 0.46 mi between the Long Ridge junction and the head of the Dodger Point Primitive Trail; its continuation to the abandoned trail end on Ludden Peak (4,940 ft per WTA 2005) has no published distance or coordinates.

Bailey Range off-trail legs have no published distances; miles are null except trip-report GPS day totals (Backcountry Post: Stephen Lake-Ferry Basin 4.83 mi/+3,137 ft; Ferry Basin-Bear Pass 5.13 mi/+2,806 ft; Bear Pass-Chicago-Hayes River 15.6 mi). The 6.6-mi Bear Pass-Chicago Camp day is derived (15.6 minus 9.0 mi Chicago-Hayes River). Several Bailey Range trip reports date from 2002-2020 and may be stale, especially for the shrinking Elwha Snowfinger.

Coordinates for Mount Carrie camps, Lone Tree (Pulitzer) Pass, Scott-Ludden Saddle, the Ludden Peak way-trail end and the Elwha Snowfinger are unknown (null). Boston Charlie's Camp, Eleven Bull Basin, Stephen Lake and Lake Billy Everett coordinates come from OpenStreetMap.

Bailey Range camp zones (Boston Charlie's, Mt Carrie Sites, etc.) are listed by Recreation.gov under a "Bailey Range" district; whether they are bookable online in 2026 vs by phone only is unclear (permit text says contact the WIC for cross-country trips).
Grand Pass elevation: DEM 6,420 ft at the NPS trail vertex, GNIS point DEM 6,366, WTA lists 6,450 as the Grand Valley high point. Obstruction Point: NPS 6,100, DEM 6,115.
Mount Angeles summit route distance (~0.6 mi from the trail fork) is derived from the WTA 6.25-mi round trip, not measured.
Happy Lake Ridge Trailhead elevation: NPS lists 1,300 ft but DEM at the mapped trailhead is ~1,740 ft.

Hurricane Ridge to Klahhane Ridge: the NPS brochure "3.8 mi one way" ends at Victor Pass (the ridge), while WTA's Klahhane Ridge hike is from the Switchback Trailhead (5.0 mi RT); the "Klahhane Ridge" node here is the Lake Angeles Trail junction ~1.2 mi farther east.
Clallam Transit 2026 shuttle end-of-season date and timetable not confirmed; Clallam Transit is a public agency (real name kept).
The Olympic Hot Springs Road long-term access decision (2019 EA) and any reopening schedule were not found; treat the road as closed to cars indefinitely.
Recreation.gov availability for summer months (July-August) could not be retrieved retroactively; Grand Valley quota numbers come from the October 2026 snapshot and may differ in peak season.

Dodwell-Rixon Pass naming (for USGS surveyors Arthur Dodwell and Theodore Rixon, who surveyed the Olympic Forest Reserve around 1898-1900) is from general knowledge, not a source fetched for this file; the origin of the name Boston Charlie's Camp is unknown.
Drive times are OSRM routing estimates (gravel Obstruction Point Road likely slower in reality; summer entrance-station waits not included).
